column1: # K2 (plan_server_novalve.md, plan_client_novalve.md): types read by layout across the
# engine/DLL boundary, compiled from the pristine upstream headers and from the DLL's
# include set (server.so's R5 set; every set client.so compiles with), layouts diffed by
# tools/abi-parity. side<TAB>type<TAB>header as #included<TAB>why it is read by layout[<TAB>options].
# Client types the plan listed and that are NOT rows, measured at c6c53802 (each is
# a row the day something reads it by layout again):
#   CPlayerState  no client TU holds one: C_StandalonePlayer and its CPlayerState are
#   kbutton_t     the engine asks IN_IsKeyDown(name, isdown) and gets a bool BY VALUE
#                 IManagedInputClient::InputIsKeyDown and writes the bool). kbutton_t
#                 is client-internal. Since C6 (lane c6-input) its state is managed's
#                 (KeyButton.cs); shell_input.cpp keeps nine kbutton_t objects only as
#                 address tokens for native callers (KeyState(&in_forward)), and nothing
#                 reads one by layout on either side.
#   CUserCmd      the engine never reads one from the DLL: IBaseClientDLL's three user-
#                 command entry points take only a bit buffer and slot numbers
#                 bf_read&, slot ); shell_clientdll.cpp forwards each to shell_input.cpp's
#                 codec of the same name), so the codec WRITES THE ENGINE'S BIT BUFFER
#                 and the ring stays in client.so. IInput, which hands out CUserCmd
#                 pointers (GetUserCmd), is not an exposed interface (shell_input.cpp
#                 has no EXPOSE_*); its only callers are client.so's own prediction.
#                 Managed gets and gives a field copy (SourceSharpUserCmd /
#                 CreateMove). Re-checked at C6's close (integrator's K2 ruling): no
#                 struct goes to the engine by pointer, so no row. A row is owed the day
#   SourceSharpInputMailbox  not an engine type: the block between client.so and its
#                 managed input (shell_input.cpp). Its layout is held by
#                 COMPILE_TIME_ASSERTs there and InputMailboxTests' same offsets.
